ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar and granular skin. It is distinguished by its specialized habitat on vertical rock faces.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Ponmudi Bush Frog is best identified by its unique, vivid reddish-brown iris, which distinguishes it from the pale or golden eyes of other similar *Raorchestes* species.
ai.habitat: The Ponmudi bush frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and rocky outcrops in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ponmudi bush frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the mossy rock faces and vegetation of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes graminirupes* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in rock crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ponmudi Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 900 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Ponmudi Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call, typically heard from rocky crevices or vegetation in its humid montane habitat.
